sections.text: Introduction

These procedure details the steps required to completely check
the proper operation and calibration of the
 L3WYS and L3WYaS relay. It is recommended this
procedure be carried out on yearly bases.

The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing
describes the activities required prior to testing. Some of these steps could be
performed days before the actual test. The second section Preparation for
testing describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual
tests. The third section is the actual test.

The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility of error causing
personal injury or damage to equipment.
Safety Precautions

A work permit
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable
 safety category,

Safety fence
 (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area,

Line isolation 
 is required.

Make sure that CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the
 current circuit for test current injection.
Tools and Equipment

items: ABB Relay Test set Type QZW 415.
Phase rotation meter.
Small slot screwdriver.

Test leads, 5 Amp, Clip-on ammeter, 
 Timer.

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out
Steps to Prepare for Relay Testing

items: Review technical reference material and manufacturer's manual.

Obtain copy of relay setting from field maintenance file and compare it
 with the setting on the relay.
Obtain outage for line protected by this relay.
Check that the line and bus disconnect switches are opened and tagged.

Inspect the CT secondary circuits, the VT Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCB's)
 and all cabling supplying the relaying.

sections.text: Testing the Relay

items: Carefully follow this test procedure.

Verify the test results match the relay setting, if not consult technical
 services.
Trip the circuit breaker associated with the relay.

sections.text: Preparation

items:
Using a clip on ammeter checks there is no current flowing in the L3
 relay circuits. Wires going to the rear terminals number 1, 2, 3 and 4
 should have no current flowing in them.

Carefully open the L3 relay cover and connect ammeter across one of
 the following test block terminals (Across terminal 2 or across terminal
 3,or across terminal 4. Using a small slot screw driver, turn that same
 test block pin until it is in the horizontal test Position) There should
 be no current flow in the ammeter, return the pin to the normal vertical
 (I Position) and check the other terminals.

Note: Always checks the continuity of the ammeter before
 using it in a (possible) live current circuit.

Remove the relay DC relay isolating plug ( located in the lower left
 corner of the relay

Connect the CT shorting link in the test block terminals as shown in
 figure (1).

Use a small slot screwdriver to turn all test terminals to horizontal (-)
 position.

Check all external connections to the relay are in a good condition, and
 check terminal block wires are tight.

Using the relay setting supplied by EEC and manufactures information
 check that all the appropriate settings have been correctly applied to the
 L3 relay.

Attach the multi -contact plug to the rear of the QZW415 test set and then
 connect the other end into
 L3WYS and L3WYaS relay test block terminals.
 Note: Carefully aligns the plug numbers with the matching
 test terminals.
Arrange the switches and links on the QZW 415 test set as the table below.

sections.text: Checking the Under Impedance Starting Elements

items:
Referring to the calibration curves fig 2 and the values
 calculated on the test sheet determine the %Z value corresponding to the
 relay setting of the starting element.

Turn the %Z switches on the test set to agree with calculated impedance of
 starting element.

Select single phase to ground faults by turning switch "g" to
 position 2.
Select the phase fault by Turing switch "f" to the position R.

Push down and turn the voltage control switch "n" to the on
 position "I"

Press the push button "nl" and observe that the auxiliary relay
 PA/R, PE, PtaW and tripping contactor PD will pick up.

Change the %Z which set on the test set by turning up or down the %z
 switches step by step
Press the push - button nl every step until PA/ R does not pick up.
Record this value on test sheet 1.

Repeat the above test for other phases S and T by turning switch
 "F" to S and T position respectively.

Repeat the above steps for phase to phase fault by turning switch
 "g" to position I)

sections.text:
Checking the Pick up Value for Measuring Element for Phase to
 Ground Fault

items:
Referring to the calibration curves fig 3 and the values
 calculated on the test sheet determine the %z value corresponding to the relay
 setting of the 1 st time step.

Turn the %z switches on the test set to agree with calculated zone 1
 setting.
Select single phase to ground faults by turning "g" to position 2

Select the phase fault by turning switch "f' to the positions R, S, and
 T respectively.

Push down and turn the voltage control switch "n" to the on
 position " I ".

Press push button (nl) and observe when " PA/R, PEW and tripping
 contactor PD " pick up (the red trip indicator lamp on the test set will
 light when the tripping contactor operates).

Change the %Z which set on the test set by turning up the %z switches step
 by step until PS 11 pick up with PA/R , PE , and the tripping contactor PD. 
 Note : PTaW does not pick up.
Repeat the above test 3 times to determine the average pick up point.
Record the pick up point for this phase to ground on test sheet 1.
Repeat the above test for the other phases S, T

Repeat the above test once again but this time increase %z
 setting on the tester until the relay operates in the 2nd time step. The
 contactor PS 11 will pick up with the above flag and PTaW
 does not pick up. Change the %Z which set on the
 test set by turning up the %z switches step by step until PS
 III pick up with PA/R, PE, and the tripping contactor PD

Repeat the above test once again but this time increase %z setting on the
 tester until the relay operate in the third time step. The contactor PS III
 will pick up with the above flag and PTaW does not pick
 up. Change the %Z which set on the test set by turning up the %Z switches step by step until the relay operate in last time step, the contactor
 PD will pick up by the fourth time contact of timer.

Press push button (nl) and observe when " PA/R, PA/T, and tripping
 contactor PD will pick up.

Change the %Z which set on the test set by turning up the %z switches step by 
 step until PS 11 will pickup with last flag. Note : PTaW does not pick up.
Record the pick up point on test sheet 1.
Repeat the above test but change switch F for the other phases (S T)

Repeat the above test once again but this time increase %z setting on the
 tester until the relay operates in the 2nd time step. The contactor PS
 11 will pick up with the above flag. Change the %Z which
 set on the test set by turning up the %z switches step by step until PS
 III pick up with PA/R, PE, and the tripping contactor PD.

Repeat the above test once again but this time increase %z setting on the
 tester until the relay operate in the third time step. The contactor PS III
 will pick up with the above flag. Change the %Z which set on the test set by
 turning up the %z switches step by step until the relay operate in last time
 step, the contactor PD will pick up by the fourth time contact of timer.

sections.text: Checking Tripping Times

General: originally the operating times of the L3 relay
 components were checked using Multi Amp. Timer connected to the QZW 415
 tester.
The Following Procedure Gives the Steps for using this Timer

items:
Toggle switch " d " on the QZW 415 to the " see
 " position to select time measurement.

Use two test leads to connect the digital timer " stop " inputs
 to terminals 12 & 13 (Y1) located in the top right comer of the QZW
 tester

Use two test leads to connect the digital timer " Start " inputs
 to the terminals 3 & 4 located in the bottom right comer of QZW tester
 just above switch n..
Connect an AC supply to the digital timer circuit.
Press the reset button for the digital timer display.
Time tests for phase to ground faults

Repeat the test of checking the Pick up Value for Measuring Element for
 Phase to Ground Fault from steps 1 to 5 as given above to measure the Zone I
 operation time for each phase to ground unit.

sections.text:
Note: Set the line impedance %Z switches to the value which
 equals half of the normal operation of the zone I Impedance.

items: To perform the time test press and turn switch nI in the closed position.

Press down and turn voltage control switch n to the on position (I) the
 time will start and then stop once the PD trip relay has picked up.
Record the time which appear on the timer display on test sheet 1.
Repeat the above test for the other two phases

Repeat the above test but change %Z setting on the QZW 415 tester to a
 value = (%Z1) + (%Z2 - % Z1) /2 until the relay operate in the 2 nd Zone
 time.

Repeat the above test but change %Z setting on the QZW 415 tester to a
 value = (%Z2) + (%Z3 - % Z2) /2 until the relay operate in the third Zone
 time.

Repeat the above test but change %Z setting on the QZW 415 tester to a
 value = (%Z3) + (%Z4 - % Z3) /2 until the relay operate in the starting Zone
 time.

Remove the DC isolating plug from the relay to de energize the
 DC circuits.
Time tests for the ph - ph unit

Select phase to phase faults by turning switch " g " to position
 " I ", and perform time tests for the phase to phase unit by
 repeating the above steps.

Remove the DC isolating plug from the relay to de energize the d.c
 circuits.
Switch off the testers.
Remove all the test lead between the relay and the tester.

sections.text: Return Relay and Associated Equipment to Service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the
 relay terminal block and the test set.
Make sure CT and VT secondary circuits are in normal condition.

If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated, it should be
 returned to service by the following restoration steps:
 - Breaker trip coils.
 - Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
 - Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.

sections.text: Request Power Line to be returned in Service

items:
Take crossed readings of all AC currents and voltages and compare them to
 those for normal load condition

Check that these reading agree with station meters (MW, MVAR, Amperes and
 Power factor)
Place a copy of the test result in the field maintenance file.
